body.x: The demand for reliable and secure elections has never been more apparent than ever. Following the January 6 United States Capitol attack to the most recent siege of Brazil's Capitol, the tension surrounding a just election has been accelerating catastrophically. Indeed, the call for fair elections goes beyond the realm of politics but also includes reality TV shows where only a year ago, the South Korean courts prosecuted two executive producers for rigging votes for a popular K-Pop survival show.

Yet last week, CES, the world's most influential tech event, finally found the answer in a small start-up company called Zkrypto. "zkVoting" is one of Zkrypto’s products, as the world's first public blockchain voting service to ensure complete voter privacy and election transparency. At CES's opening ceremony, Kinsey Fabrizio, CTA's Senior Vice President of Membership, CES Sales, and Marketing, praised zkVoting for its ability to reshape online privacy and anticipated zkVoting's ability to "usher in a whole new era for elections." Furthermore, Fabrizio announced zkVoting as "one of the three breakthrough technologies to influence and solve today's challenges.“

The CES Innovation Awards program honours outstanding design and engineering products that will lead world technologies. In addition to being awarded the Innovation Award from the software and mobile app category, zkVoting is the first ever blockchain service to be selected and recognized with the "Best of Innovation" award.

body.x: Professor Hyun-ok Oh and Professor Jihye Kim co-founded Zkrypto, which first began as a collaborative research project and later progressed into a start-up to possess Korea's top zero-knowledge-proof schemes and protocols. Zero-knowledge proof is a cryptographic privacy solution that allows a party (the prover) to guarantee the truth of specific information to another party(the verifier) without disclosing any additional information. zkVoting optimizes zero-knowledge proof to protect voters' personal information on the public blockchain whilst validating the correctness of ballot content, allowing individuals to vote with full confidence anytime and anywhere.

Professor Hyun-ok Oh, CEO of Zkrypto, commented, "By creating a permanent proof encryption for a 'one person one vote' scheme, voters can confirm their ballot in the tally but cannot know the identity and location of other voters." He further explains, "The public blockchain allows everyone to check the election process, for example, confirming whether votes are tallied and processed correctly into the ballot box." In fact, Professor Oh shares Kinsey Fabrizio's notion as he referred, "We were delighted to hear that Fabrizio and the behalf of the CTA shared our view that zkVoting will incite an unprecedented legacy for elections. Reducing election costs and ensuring a secure yet valid election will achieve societal transparency that encourages and reflects the people's will and opinion."

Professor Jihye Kim, CTO of Zkrypto, added, "We have also received a lot of attention and support from Web 3.0 industry attendees in our ability to prove that privacy-preserving services in blockchain go beyond and above infamously speculative crypto-related ecosystems. We utilize the succinct security of a public blockchain and resolve previous privacy issues with our zero-knowledge protocol." To end, Professor Kim revealed her ambition: "I will continue my research and wish to optimize zero-knowledge proofs further to tackle privacy concerns in personal data transactions, DIDs and logistics systems to create a safe and secure world.“
